CBS Sports' Pete Prisco has picked against the Panthers all season, his seeming disdain for the franchise refusing to go away. He isn't changing his ways this week, either, picking the Eagles to win by three despite giving ample reason the Panthers should win. "The Panthers are off a bye, while the Eagles are off a trip to London where they lost in brutal fashion to the Jaguars. This is desperation time for the Eagles, but the injuries have piled up. Somehow, though, they will get off the deck to win this behind their defense," he wrote. His CBS colleague, Jordan Dajani, disagreed, picking the Panthers to win 23-21. "The Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS," Dajani pointed out. Here's how SI's staff is picking the game: Albert Breer: Panthers Eva Geitheim: Panthers Mitch Goldich: Eagles Mike Kadlick: Panthers Gilberto Manzano: Panthers Conor Orr: Eagles John Pluym: Eagles Matt Verderame: Eagles Bleacher Report's Wes O'Donnell is taking the Panthers to cover the spread and win outright. "I'm done trying to figure out the Eagles. The Eagles clearly cannot figure out the Eagles. And while the Panthers' defense is a great opportunity for any offense to get right, Carolina had a bye week and then some to prepare for Philly. This Panthers team has defied the odds and shown up in tough situations since last season," he wrote. Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales reacts after the game at Bank of America Stadium | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. His colleagues Gary Davenport, Kristopher Knox, Moe Moton, and Brent Sobleski agree, while Ian Hanford and Brad Gagnon disagree, picking the Eagles. At ESPN , only Pam Maldonado and Dan Graziano picked the Eagles to beat the Panthers. The Athletic's Vic Tafur was obscenely blunt: "The Eagles are coming off two heartbreaking losses, they struggle against play-action passes (a Panthers staple), and it wouldn’t shock me if this is Sirianni’s last game as head coach." What does this mean? Despite the overwhelming advantages the Panthers have in this game, there's still a perception that the Eagles are the Eagles and the Panthers are the woeful Panthers. That makes Week 6's contest a perfect opportunity to reshape the narrative, although it's a little unfair that a primetime victory over the Detroit Lions didn't do that for the Panthers. Not only have the offensive injuries racked up in a major way for Philadelphia, but its numbers continue to be amongst the worst in the NFL. The Eagles are 29th in EPA per play and 24th in opponent EPA per play, putting them in the bottom handful of teams in the entire NFL. They're also dead last in success rate and 22nd in opponent success rate. They've somehow managed to play in close games all season, but unless they fix things in a hurry, they're going to start racking up some ugly losses. Meanwhile, the Panthers' offense is a top-10 unit. They still have some issues on defense, but their offense alone makes me think they should be favored in this NFC matchup. I'll back the Panthers as underdogs on the moneyline. Pick: Panthers +104 via FanDuel The Eagles put everything they had into last week’s game and still came up short. away.headline: Carolina Panthers HC Dave Canales has an uncomfortable decision to consider after veteran's impressive return
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers won ugly against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday and a big story coming out of the game was the return of two veteran stalwarts in the trenches who played very well in their first game back in right tackle Taylor Moton and defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton. Moton’s return couldn’t have come at a better time. While Moton was sidelined, rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling served as the team’s starting right tackle over the first four games. However, Freeling suffered a knee injury in Week 4 and wasn’t able to play on Sunday, opening the door for Moton to step back into his starting spot. Once Freeling is cleared, that’s where the conversation gets interesting. The Panthers would like to continue developing Freeling and have him out on the field. But, Moton isn’t a player you’re taking off the field and left tackle Rasheed Walker is coming off his best game of the season after allowing one pressure on 46 pass-blocking snaps. “There’s a bunch of scenarios we’re still working through,” Canales explained. “T-Mo looked like T-Mo, Rasheed Walker played his best game, we’ll see where Monroe is at physically. And we’ll go from there. This is a first-round pick for us, this is a high value player for us. We’re going to do what’s best for the Panthers and put the best group and healthiest group out there. home.headline: NFL fans demand investigation into Philadelphia Eagles' medical staff
home.blurb: The Eagles are likely to be without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, as he’s being put on blood thinners, the team announced on Monday. Hurts missed this past Sunday’s game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot. He had previously played in a loss to the Jaguars in London earlier this month. “Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition. Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. ‘blood thinners’). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football,” the team announced. “Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects. We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery.” Hurts last played in a loss to the Jaguars in London. He threw for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss. NFL insider Tom Pelissero reports that Hurts stayed up for about 36 hours straight before that game, after being diagnosed. “How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? After initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, doctors told him not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, throwing for 220 yards and a TD,” he reported. NFL fans, though, are shocked that the Eagles let him play in London. Fans are demanding a full investigation into how the team handled the Hurts injury situation. Fans demand ‘investigation’ into Hurts’ medical situation NFL fans are pushing for the league to investigate what really happened here. “WHY DID THEY LET HIM PLAY,” one NFL fan wondered on X. “A lot of people in the eagles organization should be fired for how this hurts situation was handled,” one fan added. “This is not an uplifting story, this is systemic malpractice that should lead to NFL altering consequences,” another fan wrote on X. “Not to sleep is crazy. Being told not to sleep and then playing a football game later just doesn’t make sense,” one fan added. The important thing is that Hurts will be OK, but it’ll be interesting to see what comes from this moving forward.

The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers. As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Steelers 24, Bucs 20 The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers. I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays. I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win. Overall Record: 3-2 James Hill, Writer: Steelers 21, Bucs 17 I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend. Overall record: 2-3 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 21, Steelers 14 So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week. Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon. Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win. Logan Robinson, Founder: Steelers 31, Bucs 24 This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh. I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season. I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter. River Wells, Editor: Steelers 24, Bucs 17 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better. The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters. On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too. The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it. Consensus: Steelers 4, Bucs 1 The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year? picks.blurb: Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball sign up 49ers keep rolling Rays heading to World Series Reese, Dream get even Hurts reportedly out for season Prediction For Buccaneers' Week 6 Clash Against the Pittsburgh Steelers (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Jason Klingensmith Sun, October 18, 2026 at 6:13 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally got their first victory of the season last week, but must go on a winning streak in order to make it meaningful. At 1-4, the Bucs are only 1.5 games behind the Carolina Panthers in the weak NFC South division. However, Tampa must win a few more games before it can even start thinking about making the playoffs. Luckily, the Bucs have winnable games on the schedule over the next few weeks, including a pair against division rivals. However, Tampa has the Pittsburgh Steelers on the docket next, already the Bucs' third game against an AFC North foe. The Steelers are 3-2 and have been inconsistent this season, although their offense has turned a corner after a very slow start. The Bucs are 2.5-point underdogs at home, but managed to pull off the upset against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 as 9.5-point underdogs. Beating the Steelers will qualify as an upset, but it is a very winnable game for the Bucs. Aside from a non-existent pass rush, the Bucs' defense has been very good this season. Now it must contend with a red-hot Aaron Rodgers, who has thrown for three TDs in each of Pittsburgh's last three games. Steelers' RB Jaylen Warren has also been outstanding in the last three games, rushing for 127, 93, and 101 yards. He also caught an 80-yard TD last week, and his 230 receiving yards lead the team. Tampa's run defense is second in the NFL so far, and stopping Warren is one of my five keys to a Bucs' victory , as is finally getting the pass rush to show a pulse. On offense, the Bucs have a budding star in RB Bucky Irving, who is coming off a career-best 165 rushing yards and had both a rushing and a receiving TD against Dallas. For Tampa to win, Irving must continue to be the centerpiece of the offense. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will be making his third straight start while starting QB Baker Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb. Daniels has played with the poise of a seasoned veteran and earned the first victory of his career against the Cowboys. For Tampa to win, Daniels must once again play a clean, turnover-free game. The offensive line must keep Pittsburgh's pass rush, especially T.J. Watt, away from Daniels. This game is set to be a matchup of strengths against strengths. Warren is sixth in the NFL in rushing yards and will be going up against Tampa's strong run defense. Rodgers has been great over the last three weeks, but will have to make plays against a secondary that has shut down the star WR duos of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Steelers will be without WRs Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson in this game. If Irving can get going early, it will make life much easier for Daniels, whose ability to also make plays with his legs can be a huge factor, especially on third down. This game seems like it could go either way, with a turnover or missed kick looming large at game's end. I don't think it will be Chase McLaughlin who misses the kick, as he has been perfect this season for the Bucs. Prediction: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 22

away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. home.blurb: Baker Mayfield Eyeing Return for Panthers Game? NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers. This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up. Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it. Buccaneers' Todd Bowles Rules Out 2 Players vs. Steelers This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/buccaneers/onsi as New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers . The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback. Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover. This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon. Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay. Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well. Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs. Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long. away.headline: Rams Make Decision on Blake Grupe Following Injury vs Cardinals
away.blurb: Grupe had one field goal opportunity against the Arizona Cardinals in Sunday's loss, converting from 44 yards in the first quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, he pushed returner Devin Duvernay out of bounds, suffering a knee injury in the process . He immediately came out of the game, doubtful to return, and left the stadium in a leg brace. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Grupe tore his ACL. Reporting from Los Angeles Tuesday, October 20 LA Sports Report Daily inbox intelligence from LA Sports Report Dodgers More teams ▾ Angels Galaxy LAFC Angel City The Los Angeles Rams placed kicker Blake Grupe, who signed with the team Tuesday, on injured reserve following an injury he sustained Sunday. The Rams are yet to replace him on the roster. What Happened to the Rams' Kicking Unit? Los Angeles felt Grupe's absence in the loss, as they strayed away from kicking for most of the remainder of the game. They opted to go for two following a second-quarter touchdown, failing the attempt, and turned the ball over on downs on the Cardinals' 27-yard line in the third quarter rather than kicking a 44-yard field goal. Punter Ethan Evans hit a PAT to give the Rams a one-point lead with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter, but the Cardinals stormed down the field to hit a field goal and win by a score of 18-16. This incident came less than a week after the Rams waived their previous kicker, Harrison Mevis , due to his inaccuracy in last week's Monday Night Football loss to the Buffalo Bills. Neither of Mevis' two looks last week went through the sticks, one being a game-tying effort in overtime, which the Bills blocked. Without a kicker on their roster, the Rams are sure to make a pickup with Grupe sidelined. The Rams are off to a rough start to the season, as they currently have a 2-4 record through six games and sit last in the NFC West. Despite their sour record, though, the Rams have been among the best offensively and defensively in the NFL. They'll get an opportunity to bounce back from a rough few weeks on Sunday, when they face off against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have lost each of their last three games following a 3-0 start. Kickoff for that game comes at 1:25 p.m. PT. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona's offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. away.headline: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love sits Wednesday
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.headline: Despite Rams’ awful start, devastating injuries, Super Bowl run still in the cards
home.blurb: Let’s just come right out and ask what everyone is thinking: Is the Rams season already over? Even questionable late-game officiating involving Josh Wallace in two losses cannot excuse everything that happened before those decisive moments. They are 2-4 this year, but with three Wild Card spots available, and the NFC looking mostly like a dumpster fire, just reaching the playoffs is not crazy difficult to attain. Skip to main content Primary Menu Sections US News Metro Switch between CA and NY editions here. CA NY Open NFL navigation Sports Sports See more of our coverage in your search results. Well, the Los Angeles Rams apparently never got the memo because not only did they lose to the Arizona Cardinals on the scoreboard on Sunday afternoon, but also on the injury report that was revealed on Monday. The Cardinals delivered a humiliating 18-16 defeat that dropped the Rams to 2-4 and into last place in the NFC West. Then, less than 24 hours later, they were dealt another brutal blow when head coach Sean McVay revealed an avalanche of injuries that was somehow more devastating than the final score. Newly signed kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL making a touchdown-saving tackle after another special teams coverage breakdown. Star receiver Davante Adams ruptured his semitendinosus near his left knee and faces surgery and a six-to-10-week absence. Nose tackle Poona Ford ruptured his triceps and is finished for the season, while defensive end Kobie Turner suffered a groin strain that will sideline him for several weeks. Add those names to a growing injury list featuring Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Trent McDuffie, and the Rams now look more like a MASH unit than a team with Super Bowl aspirations. Let’s face it, if there were ever a time to burn sage inside SoFi Stadium and perform an exorcism, this might be it. Between the Rams' misfortunes and the Chargers' 0-6 start, things could not get any worse for NFL teams in Los Angeles. At the NFL level, everyone is getting paid to do their job. It has to be a next man up mentality.” At some point, the phrase “next man up” stops sounding inspirational and starts sounding like a desperate plea for healthy bodies. Safety Quentin Lake echoed that sentiment, emphasizing the importance of keeping injured teammates involved while preparing their replacements. “It's now next man up, guys are going to be able to come in and make an impact,” Lake said. home.headline: Rams Make Decision on Blake Grupe Following Injury vs Cardinals
home.blurb: Grupe had one field goal opportunity against the Arizona Cardinals in Sunday's loss, converting from 44 yards in the first quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, he pushed returner Devin Duvernay out of bounds, suffering a knee injury in the process . He immediately came out of the game, doubtful to return, and left the stadium in a leg brace. ESPN's Adam Schefter reports Grupe tore his ACL. Reporting from Los Angeles Tuesday, October 20 LA Sports Report Daily inbox intelligence from LA Sports Report Dodgers More teams ▾ Angels Galaxy LAFC Angel City The Los Angeles Rams placed kicker Blake Grupe, who signed with the team Tuesday, on injured reserve following an injury he sustained Sunday. The Rams are yet to replace him on the roster. What Happened to the Rams' Kicking Unit? Los Angeles felt Grupe's absence in the loss, as they strayed away from kicking for most of the remainder of the game. They opted to go for two following a second-quarter touchdown, failing the attempt, and turned the ball over on downs on the Cardinals' 27-yard line in the third quarter rather than kicking a 44-yard field goal. Punter Ethan Evans hit a PAT to give the Rams a one-point lead with less than a minute left in the fourth quarter, but the Cardinals stormed down the field to hit a field goal and win by a score of 18-16. This incident came less than a week after the Rams waived their previous kicker, Harrison Mevis , due to his inaccuracy in last week's Monday Night Football loss to the Buffalo Bills. Neither of Mevis' two looks last week went through the sticks, one being a game-tying effort in overtime, which the Bills blocked. Without a kicker on their roster, the Rams are sure to make a pickup with Grupe sidelined. The Rams are off to a rough start to the season, as they currently have a 2-4 record through six games and sit last in the NFC West. Despite their sour record, though, the Rams have been among the best offensively and defensively in the NFL. They'll get an opportunity to bounce back from a rough few weeks on Sunday, when they face off against the Las Vegas Raiders, who have lost each of their last three games following a 3-0 start. Kickoff for that game comes at 1:25 p.m. PT. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 6 vs Rams
home.blurb: A groin issue was tacked on to safety Budda Baker's rest designation. The safety did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable for the weekend. Zaven Collins also did not practice with a hip issue and is questionable. The other players questionable are punter Blake Gillikin (back) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). The Cardinals could activate Crawford to the roster by tomorrow afternoon. After not practicing all week, the team ruled out running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and safeties Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) and Dewey Wingard (knee). Quarterback Carson Beck had a back injury that made him limited on Friday. He did not receive a game designation. Sean McVay said cornerback Trent McDuffie pulled his groin at practice on Thursday and is listed as questionable. Safety Kam Curl is also questionable with a ankle issue. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not take part in practice on Thursday as he allows his ankle to heal. It's also looking bleak for safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) to play after logging another DNP. It was another limited practice for wide receiver Devin Duvernay (ribs) and safety Kitan Crawford (ankle). While game designations will be announced on Friday, the Cardinals have until Saturday to activate Crawford to the main roster if they want him to play this weekend. The Rams practiced for the first time this week. Safety Kam Curl was limited with an ankle injury. The ankle issue continues to linger for Jeremiyah Love. While the Cardinals running back has played through the discomfort, he did not practice on Wednesday. Coach Mike LaFleur emphasized caution and rest. Safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) also did not practice ahead of the Week 6 game against the Rams. Williams would need to progress through concussion protocol to play. Kitan Crawford had his 21-day practice window opened and returned to practice after exiting Week 1 with an ankle injury. He was limited. Wide receiver/returner Devin Duvernay (ribs) was also limited. picks.blurb: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group. With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like. Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season. If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe. Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances. Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters. Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles. This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender. The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart. The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising. Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.

home.headline: Chargers Injury Report: Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston off report vs. Chiefs
home.blurb: Hurts reportedly out for season Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston were both completely taken off the injury report and should be ready to roll against the Chiefs. Fellow wideouts KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Brenen Thompson were both listed as questionable but both should also be in line to return to the field, though KLS still needs to be activated officially off of IR before Sunday. The other players listed as questionable are defensive tackle Jamaree Caldwell, edge rusher Bud Dupree, linebacker Daiyan Henley, and defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson. Cornerback Rodney Shelley is the lone player with a doubtful tag. Offensive tackle Joe Alt, guard Kayode Awosika, wide receiver Tre' Harris, cornerback Donte Jackson, and safety Derwin James were all ruled out for Sunday. This will be the third missed game for James and the second missed game for Alt who is still receiving opinions on his neck injury he sustained against the Seahawks. *Note that Bud Dupree is listed as both questionable and out. We'll wait for further clarification before adjusting the report. In the second straight practice, the team had LT Josh Simmons participate in a limited capacity . Rashee Rice missed his second straight practice , putting him on track to miss the Week 6 game against Los Angeles. Andy Reid typically requires players to participate in one limited practice to play in a game. One new defensive development: Rookie DT Peter Woods missed practice with an injury. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's second Week 6 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 16. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Chiefs rookie DT Peter Woods was added to the injury report with a neck injury after participating fully on Wednesday. He was not on the injury report in any capacity on Wednesday, but was listed as limited on Thursday. Based on what we know, he could've hurt himself during practice on Wednesday or Thursday. His practice status on Friday will determine his availability for Sunday. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' first injury report for Week 6 tilt vs. Los Angeles Chargers shows a team on the mend after the bye week
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their first injury report ahead of Week 6 against the Los Angeles Chargers. After having 10 players on the final injury report ahead of the Week 5 bye, Kansas City's roster appears to be on the mend. Rashee Rice didn't participate in practice on Wednesday, but the team removed 5 players who were hurt just two weeks ago from the injury report. For the first time since mid-August, Chiefs LT Josh Simmons took part in a limited practice session. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team's first Week 6 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. They will release game status designations on Friday, Oct. 16. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related As Coach Reid said, Rice did not participate, and Simmons participated in a limited capacity. Simmons moved gingerly in video taken during the open portion of practice ( see FOX 4's footage here ). The Kansas City Chiefs return from their earliest bye of the Patrick Mahomes era facing a 13-week stretch run. A thin wide receiver room and a few rising young players will change the rotation. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Everything you need to know to catch this AFC matchup Imagn Images The Buffalo Bills were expected to be one of the best teams in the AFC, while the Las Vegas Raiders were, well ... not. However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0. Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season. The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4. Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo. Bills vs. Raiders: need to know Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3. Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8. Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league. Bills vs. Raiders: where to watch Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ET Location: Allegiant Stadium (Las Vegas) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -5.5 ( via DraftKings ) Bills vs. Raiders prediction The Raiders were put in a difficult stretch, facing the Chiefs, Patriots and Bills back-to-back-to-back. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. While he recovered in time for the regular season, the issue has continued to linger, making it difficult for him to play at full strength. Jeanty appeared to aggravate the ankle during Las Vegas' Week 4 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs before dealing with an additional foot issue ahead of last Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots.

Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. The Las Vegas Raiders received encouraging news regarding Ashton Jeanty's health as the team prepares for Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era Getty Images One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night. Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half. However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research. Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary . Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch: Where to watch Cowboys vs. Packers Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Cowboys vs. Packers need to know Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season. This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019. Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it. How fixable are the issues? "Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable." Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees. "Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things. Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs. "We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this." Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards. In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006. Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense. A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious. New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers. Cowboys vs. Packers prediction Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams . However, Dallas' defense struggles will limit their offense's ability to find a rhythm. The Cowboys are averaging 3.07 points per drive, the second-highest by a team under .500 through five games this century per CBS Sports Research, but their 45 drives this season are the second fewest in the league this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Dallas has the No. 32 defense in the league in EPA/Play, success rate and yards per play allowed, putting a ton of pressure on Dak Prescott and Co. to score on just about every possession. The result for Sunday’s game? A total in the 50s and a very close spread between two teams that have some work to do if they want to make the postseason in the NFC. So, how should we bet on it? away.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

away.headline: Cowboys Floated as Spot for Bill Belichick NFL Return
away.blurb: Former Cowboys scout Bryan Broaddus raised the topic on the station, pointing out that UNC is 4-2 this season and saying, “Belichick has actually got North Carolina playing well. And now, is it one of those situations where it is like a way to get Bill back in the league?” Said Dawson: “It might be best-case scenario if you’re a Cowboys fan, if they moved on from Schotty. All the things that we’ve talked about … over the years, the criteria what a guy has to have and make habits out of for Jerry to hire him. I think Belichick would be best-case scenario. Just Monday, Stephen Jones was on the radio offering support to Schottenheimer when asked if the team remains committed to the coach : “Absolutely. There’s not any question in Jerry and I’s mind the team, he has the team, there’s no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen and I feel really good about our coaching staff, we just have to continue to have it evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games.” The post Cowboys Floated as Spot for Bill Belichick NFL Return appeared first on HEAVY . It’s a longshot of course, but if the Dallas Cowboys brain trust of Jerry and Stephen Jones did decide sometime soon that hiring a guy–like current coach Brian Schottenheimer–who is big on palling around with and “loving on” (as he likes to say) players, but short on NFL heft as far as his resume and his background go, then there’s at least a chance the team could land his direct opposite. That would be the ever-grimacing Bill Belichick, the sure bet Hall of Famer who was let go by the Patriots after the 2023 season and who has begun to turn around his wayward North Carolina program this season. Belichick has six Super Bowl rings, and 333 wins as an NFL head coach. That’s a much different background than Schottenheimer had when he was promoted from offensive coordinator to replace Mike McCarthy before the 2025 season. While there was chatter among the NFL’s observer class that the Cowboys would pursue Belichick to replace McCarthy before that, such a pursuit never really came to fruition. But if Schottenheimer does not survive this season, could Dallas reconsider and actually make a run at Belichick? Bill Belichick Could Want Back in the NFL That’s the theory that was floated over at 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday, following the 23-13 loss to the Packers on Sunday that sent the Cowboys’ record to a measly 2-4 and dropped Schottenheimer to 9-13-1 as a head coach. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week.
