More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. Receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) does not have an status designation and will play. How will the injury situation affect Sunday night's showdown with the Cowboys? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 6: OL Jacob Monk (quad): He's no longer a starting option at right guard, where Travis Glover or Kevin Zeitler will start Sunday, but Monk could be a backup at center and get snaps on special teams protection units if he's healthy. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. DL Javon Hargrave (Achilles): The veteran suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury last Sunday and will eventually go on injured reserve, possibly as soon as Saturday. CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring)

home.headline: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report
home.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

home.headline: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers
home.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. Packers Rule Out Four, Including Javon Hargrave Green Bay ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave , receiver Skyy Moore , and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste . Defensive tackle Jordon Riley , who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, is doubtful with an Achilles injury. Guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee and toe injury, along with defensive tackle Anthony Campbell with an ankle injury, cornerback Brandon Cisse with a hip injury added Friday, center/guard Jacob Monk with a quadriceps injury, and receiver Savion Williams , who has an ankle injury and is also in his return window. ‘I Just Kept Throwing Up’: Joey Porter Jr. Details Illness That Kept Him Out Against Buccaneers, Targets Green Bay A New Ankle Listing For Joey Porter Jr. Full Go For CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, And Alijah Clark Safety Alijah Clark , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, practiced fully all three days and carries no game status. So did left tackle Tyler Guyton with a back injury, outside linebacker James Houston with a shoulder injury, receiver CeeDee Lamb with a thigh injury, cornerback Shavon Revel with a knee injury, and left guard Tyler Smith with his surgically repaired thumb. Lamb said Thursday that his thigh bruise started in the second quarter of the Cowboys’ win at Houston and that he was back to square one after the mini-bye. Cornerback Keisean Nixon , edge rusher Lukas Van Ness , safety Evan Williams , and defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt carry no game status. Micah Parsons , who is recovering from a torn ACL, is not on the report. Kickoff at Lambeau Field is set for 7:20 p.m. CT on Sunday, Oct. 18, on NBC. Save my name, email, and website in

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights San Francisco can improve to 6-0 and strengthen its NFC West lead, while Washington enters Levi's Stadium looking to pull off a sizable road upset Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Monday Night Football," the San Francisco 49ers play host to the Washington Commanders . San Francisco is riding high atop the NFC West with a 5-0 record, having defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in a barnburner last week. The Niners have battled injuries on both sides of the ball all season, yet have remained unbeaten. They can create a three-game lead in the division with a victory on Monday night. Washington is coming off an absolute debacle last Sunday against the New York Giants , wherein the Commanders had a chance to kick a field goal to win the game at the end of overtime, but bungled the clock management as badly as any team you'll ever see. The Commies are just 1-3-1 entering this game, and they're looking to avoid falling further into the basement in the NFC East. Will the Niners continue to roll, or will the Commanders pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch 49ers vs. Commanders live Date: Monday, Oct. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, California) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: 49ers -7.5, O/U 52.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball Jayden Daniels looked no worse for wear last week in his return from another dislocated elbow. He completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, while also rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns. Had he and the entire offense not totally brain-farted at the end of overtime, it would have been a wildly encouraging performance for Washington's rest-of-season outlook. While Daniels has been excellent when taking off to run in his three starts, Washington's running backs have been extremely inefficient on the ground. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (who was ruled out for this game after not practicing all week), Rachaad White , Austin Ekeler and the recently-released Kaytron Allen have combined to average just 3.7 yards per carry. The offensive line has created little push up front, with the backs collectively gaining just 0.95 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, and the backs themselves have broken tackles at the second-lowest rate in all of football. The 49ers, meanwhile, have allowed just 3.7 yards per rush to enemy running backs, with great tackling being the primary method of limiting yardage. Backs have gained 1.47 yards per carry before contact (an above-average mark), but only 2.22 yards after contact thanks to the lowest broken-tackle rate in the league. As a result, San Francisco has allowed only two explosive runs all season, per Tru Media, the fewest in the NFL . San Francisco has also been mostly strong against the pass, checking in 10th in opponents' EPA per dropback and 5th in opponents' success rate. The 49ers have allowed quarterbacks to complete only 64.4% of their passes at an average of 6.1 yards per attempt, with just five touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. It's tough to know what to make of Washington's passing game because it hasn't been at full strength for most of the season. Daniels missed two-and-a-half games. Chig Okonwko missed two. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs each missed one and saw their snaps limited in another. The Daniels-McLaurin-Diggs trio has shared the field for only 57 plays so far this season, according to Tru Media. Daniels is just 15 of 30 for 129 yards on those plays, but he has thrown for three scores and scrambled for 62 yards. Daniels should, in theory, see at least some clean pockets with the 49ers again playing without Nick Bosa , but Washington's offensive line has yielded pressure on over 38% of dropbacks so far this season, so the Niners could have a chance to get into Daniels' lap and force him into tough throws and mistakes. With the generally sticky coverage the San Francisco corners have played so far this season, it could be tough sledding for Washington in the passing game on Monday night. When the 49ers have the ball San Francisco has been the league's fourth-most efficient offense by EPA per play, according to Tru Media, ranking second with the pass and 14th with the run. Brock Purdy is playing at as high a level as any quarterback in football, completing 69% of his passes at an average of 8.4 yards per attempt with a league-high 13 touchdown passes and just two interceptions. Purdy also has a 57.9% passing success rate, which ranks as the best in the league. Purdy has done that despite hemorrhaging wide receivers throughout the season. Ricky Pearsall was lost for the year in training camp. Christian Kirk (listed as questionable for this week) has yet to make his 49er debut. De'Zhaun Stribling was injured in Week 1. Demarcus Robinson went down in Week 2. Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were knocked out of last week's win over the Seahawks. Mike Evans has been playing through a painful rib injury. (He's also questionable for Monday night.) George Kittle spent the first two weeks ramping up to a full workload after last season's Achilles tear. And yet, here the 49ers are. Washington, meanwhile, has been one of the league's friendliest pass defenses. Every team the Commanders have faced has thrown for at least 257 net yards. Four of the five teams have gone more than 300 and two of them exceeded 400. The Commanders have allowed opponents to complete 65.2% of passes at an average of 7.1 yards per attempt, with 14 touchdowns and just three interceptions. The 103.9 passer rating against the Commanders to date is the sixth-worst mark in the league. It's very easy to see San Francisco finding success through the air so long as Evans suits up for the game. Christian McCaffrey is sharing the workload in the run game far more this season than in years past, with 61 carries for 286 yards againt Kaelon Black's 37 carries for 136 yards. McCaffrey's 4.7 yards-per-carry average is far better than what he posted over the last two years (4.0 and 3.9), and his rushing success rate of 45.9% is seventh-best out of 48 qualifying running backs. That figure is the second-best mark of his career, behind only the 2023 season, during which he led the NFL in rushing yards. The Commanders have actually been stingy against the run this year, allowing only 3.9 yards per carry, with opposing backs limited to 0.69 yards per attempt before contact by the defensive front. Washington having similar success stopping the run here is important because it could make the 49ers one-dimensional, but the Commanders' pass-funnel defense also plays right into San Francisco's hands because of how efficient the 49ers' passing game has been so far this year. Purdy and Co. should eat, even if McCaffrey doesn't. I picked against the 49ers last week and regretted it almost immediately after seeing how their offense struggled against the stingy Seattle defense. Needless to say, Washington's defense is not of the same quality. I know the 49ers are still hemorrhaging wide receivers, but as long as Brock Purdy, Mike Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey are healthy and Kyle Shanahan is calling the plays, they are going to move the ball efficiently. And I don't trust the Commanders to do quite enough to keep up with their explosive offense. It popped up this week for the first time this season, in addition to his broken ribs from Week 3, preventing him from being even a limited participant in practice. Without Evans, and already missing four of their other top receivers, the 49ers’ offense grinded to a halt. After kicking a field goal on their first drive of the second half, San Francisco went three-and-out on three consecutive drives as Washington scored two unanswered touchdowns. “I don’t think we went three-and-out three straight times because Mike wasn’t out there,” said tight end George Kittle, who was San Francisco’ second-leading receiver with 69 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. “Obviouslly he would’ve helped. While Christian Kirk (calf) returned to practice this week and was listed as questionable to make his season debut, Shanahan said the 29-year-old was merely a “possibility” to be activated next week, the same terminology he used leading into this game. Demarcus Robinson, who suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 2, is not yet an option, Shanahan said. De’Zhaun Stribling and Deebo Samuel are even further away, and Ricky Pearsall is out for the year. SANTA CLARA — As Mike Evans goes, so go the 49ers . The 33-year-old wide receiver left their 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday night and San Francisco’s offense flat-lined to such a degree that they nearly let a 20-point lead slip away. The postgame prognosis came with good news and bad news. The not-so-positive: Brock Purdy may have to find another top target, at least in the short term. According to NBC Sports Bay Area insider Jennifer Lee Chan , Evans’ Achilles tendon remained “intact” but the 49ers were bracing for him to miss at least next week’s game in Atlanta. That conflicted with the positive spin Shanahan put on Evans’ outlook after the game. “Hopefully he’ll be able to play next week,” Shanahan said. “But if not, we’ll have to have the rest of the group step up and hopefully get him healed up after the bye week.” “Just acted up too much in the game and couldn’t go,” Shanahan said. “We’ll see how he feels this week. … Just talking to Mike, it was something he had dealt with in the past in his career. He felt confident that he’d be good today, so that was the confidence he gave me. “But we knew that he might not be able to last.” Shanahan said it was a “pretty close call” whether Evans would suit up at all against the Commanders. He ended up leading the 49ers with 93 yards on three catches, despite limping to the locker room about a minute before halftime and never returning. “We’ve just got to execute, and I don’t think we did.” Although the 49ers hung on to improve to 6-0, it wasn’t exactly an encouraging sign

home.blurb: San Francisco 49ers are getting great news at the perfect time as key playmakers are set to return from injury Skip to content Shanahan said wide receiver Christian Kirk, who has been out with a calf injury, is a “possibility” to play in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. He also said wide receiver Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks , is unlikely to return until after the Week 8 bye. Kirk suffered his calf injury in training camp and has yet to take the field this season. He was placed on injured reserve in the preseason and had his 21-day return to practice window opened on October 15th. Now he's a possibility to play against Atlanta, and I like that for two reasons. First, if Kirk doesn't play Sunday, he'll likely suit up in Week 9 when the 49ers return from the bye against the Las Vegas Raiders. If he doesn’t get activated, he must get placed on season-ending IR and it’s highly doubtful that San Francisco will let that happen. Kirk’s return could be huge for an offense that needs bodies on the outside. By holding Samuel out this week and letting the bye do its work, San Francisco essentially gives him two more weeks to recover while he misses only one more game. Hamstrings are tricky, and the last thing this team needs is a setback that lingers into November. Patience here is the smart play, and the schedule rewards it. Christian Kirk's timeline is a win either way Second, if he does suit up and is active against the Falcons, he doesn't have to carry a full workload. The 49ers can give him somewhere between 10 and 30 plays, depending on how things go. That gets one game under his belt without overloading him. Then he gets the extra time off during the bye to recover before the back half of the season. That's the beauty of this timing. San Francisco doesn't have to choose between rushing Kirk back and leaving him on the shelf. Either path works. Deebo Samuel doesn't need to be rushed The same logic applies to Samuel.
